answer: I would like to talk about a friend whose language skills I find genuinely impressive. A person who speaks a foreign language impressively well is a friend of mine who is almost [[fluent]] in Japanese, despite never having lived there. We met at university, and she is now preparing to apply for a master's degree in Japan, which is partly how we reconnected, since I helped her with her application at the consultancy where I work. Before that, we had not spoken properly for a couple of years. As for how she learned it, what amazes me is that she taught herself largely through films, music and online conversation, which shows extraordinary discipline. She practised every single day for years, even writing short diary entries in Japanese script. Her pronunciation is so [[authentic]] that native speakers are often surprised she is not from Japan. I think what makes her so good is that she was never afraid of making mistakes, which is where most learners get stuck. She immersed herself completely, treating the language as a passion rather than a chore. Watching her switch effortlessly between Bengali and Japanese is genuinely [[admirable]], and it makes me slightly envious. She often says that learning a language opens a window into a whole culture, and I think she is right. Honestly, her [[commitment]] is inspiring, and it has motivated me to be more serious about improving my own English, especially since I hope to study abroad myself one day.

followUps.q: Would you like to learn another foreign language?
followUps.answer: Yes, I would love to learn Arabic properly, since I can already read it a little from studying the Quran as a child. Understanding it fully would make my prayers feel far more meaningful.

followUps.q: Is learning English important in your country?
followUps.answer: Very important. English opens doors to higher education and better jobs, and in my work I see every day how much students' futures [[hinge on]] their English test scores.
